levels.title: High-Alert Brand Recognition
levels.description: Differentiate deceptive brand names that look and sound nearly identical.
levels.learningObjective: Identify critical clinical indication differences between deceptive brand names like Actonel and Actos.

questions.prompt: Actonel (risedronate) is dangerously confused with Actos (pioglitazone). What is the primary indication of Actonel?
questions.explanation: Actonel is a bisphosphonate for osteoporosis requiring upright positioning, whereas Actos is an oral antidiabetic agent. Dispensing errors can cause untreated diabetes or severe esophageal irritation.

questions.prompt: Which population is Adacel (Tdap) specifically formulated for, compared to pediatric Daptacel (DTaP)?
choices: Adolescents and adults (booster with reduced toxoid)
questions.correctAnswer: Adolescents and adults (booster with reduced toxoid)
questions.explanation: Adacel (Tdap) is formulated with reduced diphtheria toxoid for adolescents and adults. Daptacel (DTaP) contains full-strength toxoid and is exclusively indicated for infants and young children.

levels.title: Interactive Pair Matching
levels.description: Rapidly connect look-alike and sound-alike counterparts through tactile retrieval matching.
levels.learningObjective: Reinforce cognitive associations between confusable pairs under active retrieval conditions.

questions.prompt: Match each medication with its documented confusable counterpart:
questions.explanation: Activase and TNKase are both thrombolytics with distinct dosing protocols. Actonel treats osteoporosis while Actos treats diabetes. Adacel is for adolescents/adults (Tdap) whereas Daptacel (DTaP) is for children. Ado-trastuzumab is an antibody-drug conjugate carrying lethal toxicity if substituted for conventional trastuzumab.

levels.title: Conjugate & Formulation Safety
levels.description: Discriminate complex prefix additions and recombinant antibody-drug conjugates.
levels.learningObjective: Prevent catastrophic oncology substitution errors between ado-trastuzumab emtansine and trastuzumab.

questions.prompt: Why did the FDA and ISMP require the 'ado-' prefix for ado-trastuzumab emtansine (Kadcyla)?
choices: To prevent fatal dosing mix-ups with conventional trastuzumab (Herceptin)
To denote that it is an oral liquid formulation
Because it was manufactured in an Asian pharmaceutical facility
To signal that it is an over-the-counter biosimilar
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent fatal dosing mix-ups with conventional trastuzumab (Herceptin)
questions.explanation: Ado-trastuzumab emtansine is an antibody-drug conjugate with cytotoxic payload. Substituting it at conventional trastuzumab doses has caused fatal overdoses, leading ISMP to require distinct prefix differentiation.

questions.prompt: Advair (fluticasone/salmeterol) is an inhaler for asthma. What is Advicor (niacin/lovastatin) indicated for?
questions.explanation: Advair is an oral inhaler for asthma and COPD, whereas Advicor is an oral tablet for dyslipidemia. Phonetic prescription call-in errors have led to improper dispensing.

activities.learningObjective: Independently construct the exact Tall Man lettering for acetazolamide without scaffolding.

questions.prompt: Enter the complete medication name using exact Tall Man lettering to distinguish it from acetoHEXAMIDE and acetaminophen:
questions.explanation: acetaZOLAMIDE capitalizes ZOLAMIDE to differentiate this carbonic anhydrase inhibitor from acetoHEXAMIDE and acetaminophen.
